text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. The main goal is to make code easier to read and understand. When programmers refactor, they clean up messy sections, remove duplicate parts, and give variables clearer names. This helps reduce technical debt, which builds up when quick fixes are used instead of proper solutions. Refactoring does not add new features or fix bugs; it simply makes the code neater. Teams often refactor regularly because clean code is easier to maintain, test, and update in the future.
